result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.bridges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find all bridge edges in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19880-L19952){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.bridges() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A bridge (also called a cut edge) is an edge whose removal increases the number of connected components. Bridges are critical edges that, if removed, would disconnect parts of the network. Uses Tarjan's algorithm for undirected graphs (`O(V + E)` time complexity) and strongly connected component analysis for directed graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of edge IDs that are bridges. Empty list if no bridges exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - bridges are critical for network vulnerability analysis - in a tree, all edges are bridges - in a cycle, no edges are bridges - related to articulation points (vertices whose removal disconnects the graph) ## Examples {.doc-examples} A path graph has no cycles, so removing any single edge splits it in two — every edge is a bridge: ::: {#099cbad5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(4) bridges = graph.bridges() # Returns 3 (all edges are bridges in a path) len(bridges) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Attaching a "tail" node to an otherwise cyclic graph creates exactly one bridge: the edge connecting the tail to the cycle, since the cycle itself has no bridges: ::: {#3b533cef .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(4) # 0-1-2-3-0 graph.add_node(label="tail") tail_id = graph.get_id_from_label("tail") nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) graph.add_edge(nodes[-1], tail_id) # Add a tail bridges = graph.bridges() # Returns 1 (only the edge to the tail is a bridge) len(bridges) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0 ``` ::: ::: The returned IDs can be resolved back to node pairs to see exactly which connections are critical: ::: {#0481ada5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(3) bridge_ids = graph.bridges() # Each bridge maps back to a (source, target) node pair [graph.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(eid) for eid in bridge_ids] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [(1, 2), (2, 3)] ``` ::: :::
